name: Network Security
description: Security of network protocols and infrastructure: routing, DNS, BGP, middleboxes, DDoS, and traffic analysis.
narrative:
The earliest network-security work in this set wrestled with the trust and topology of the Internet's core infrastructure. "Bamboozling Certificate Authorities with BGP" (2018) showed that BGP route hijacks could subvert the very domain-validation checks certificate authorities rely on, turning a routing weakness into a way to mint fraudulent TLS certificates, while "NetHide: Secure and Practical Network Topology Obfuscation" (2018) tackled the flip side of the same coin: hiding network structure from traceroute-style probing so attackers cannot map targets for link-flooding. Alongside these, "FANCI: Feature-based Automated NXDomain Classification and Intelligence" (2018) attacked malware command-and-control by classifying the algorithmically generated domains that botnets resolve, and "All Things Considered" (2019) gave one of the first large-scale empirical looks at the messy reality of IoT devices on real home networks.

By 2020-2021 the field shifted toward defending the data plane itself, increasingly leaning on programmable switches and protocol rigor. "Jaqen" (2021) and "Ripple" (2021) both exploited programmable switches to mount line-rate, ISP-scale defenses against volumetric DDoS and link-flooding attacks, moving mitigation from end hosts into the network fabric. In parallel, "Analysis of DTLS Implementations Using Protocol State Fuzzing" (2020) brought systematic state-machine fuzzing to a widely deployed UDP security protocol, and "NetWarden: Mitigating Network Covert Channels while Preserving Performance" (2020) showed how to shut down covert channels without paying a heavy performance tax.

The most sustained thread, though, is the cat-and-mouse game of encrypted traffic analysis, especially website fingerprinting on Tor. "Zero-delay Lightweight Defenses against Website Fingerprinting" (2020) pushed practical, low-overhead defenses, which attackers promptly countered: "Online Website Fingerprinting" (2022) and "Subverting Website Fingerprinting Defenses with Robust Traffic Representation" (2023) demonstrated attacks that hold up in realistic, real-world conditions. Defenders also borrowed from adversarial ML, as in "Defeating DNN-Based Traffic Analysis Systems in Real-Time With Blind Adversarial Perturbations" (2021).

Where the area stands now is the maturation of learning-based traffic analysis into something robust and deployable. "An Efficient Design of Intelligent Network Data Plane" (2023) runs ML classifiers directly in the data plane at line speed, and "Rosetta" (2023) makes TLS-encrypted traffic classification robust across diverse, shifting network environments through TCP-aware augmentation. Together they mark the field's move from one-off attacks and defenses toward in-network, generalizable inference on encrypted traffic.

milestones.title: Bamboozling Certificate Authorities with BGP
milestones.note: showed BGP hijacks can defeat CA domain validation and mint fraudulent TLS certificates, linking routing security to the web PKI

milestones.title: NetHide: Secure and Practical Network Topology Obfuscation
milestones.note: introduced practical topology obfuscation to blunt traceroute-based reconnaissance and link-flooding attacks

milestones.title: Analysis of DTLS Implementations Using Protocol State Fuzzing
milestones.note: brought systematic protocol state fuzzing to a widely used UDP security protocol, surfacing implementation flaws

milestones.title: Jaqen: A High-Performance Switch-Native Approach for Detecting and Mitigating Volumetric DDoS Attacks with Programmable Switches
milestones.note: moved ISP-scale volumetric DDoS defense into programmable switches at line rate

milestones.title: Ripple: A Programmable, Decentralized Link-Flooding Defense Against Adaptive Adversaries
milestones.note: used programmable data planes for decentralized defense against adaptive link-flooding adversaries

milestones.title: Online Website Fingerprinting: Evaluating Website Fingerprinting Attacks on Tor in the Real World
milestones.note: showed Tor website-fingerprinting attacks remain effective under realistic real-world conditions

milestones.title: An Efficient Design of Intelligent Network Data Plane
milestones.note: deployed ML traffic analysis directly in the data plane for line-speed inference

milestones.title: Rosetta: Enabling Robust TLS Encrypted Traffic Classification in Diverse Network Environments with TCP-Aware Traffic Augmentation
milestones.note: made encrypted-traffic classification robust across diverse network environments via TCP-aware augmentation
